nodes.description: In-frame deletions and missense variants lower ZFP36L2 protein in oocytes (attributed to instability of the variant mRNA) and weaken binding of ZFP36L2 to the CCR4-NOT deadenylase subunit CNOT6L. ZFP36L2 normally binds AU-rich elements in the 3' untranslated region of its target mRNAs and recruits CCR4-NOT to deadenylate and degrade them. The genotypes are treated as partial rather than complete loss of function because affected women have no reported somatic phenotype, and none of the reported genotypes is a predicted null.

evidence.snippet: In vitro studies showed that the variant caused decreased protein levels of ZFP36L2 in oocytes due to mRNA instability and might lead to the loss of its function to degrade maternal mRNAs.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of novel compound heterozygous ZFP36L2 variants implicated in oocyte maturation defects and female infertility.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that these variants lead to compromised binding capacity of the ZFP36L2-CONT6L complex and impaired mRNA degradation in HeLa cells and mouse oocytes.

nodes.description: Homozygous females are infertile. On the C57BL/6NTac background they ovulate and their eggs are fertilized, but embryos arrest at the two-cell stage. On a 129S6/SvEvTac background they do not ovulate and most oocytes stay at the germinal vesicle stage, a difference the authors partly attribute to strain differences in ovarian luteinizing hormone receptor mRNA, another ZFP36L2 target.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, we discovered that ZFP36L2 interacts with the 3'UTR of LHR mRNA and that decreased expression levels of Zfp36l2 correlates with higher levels of LHR mRNA in synchronized ovaries.

nodes.description: Fertilized embryos repeatedly arrest before the blastocyst stage (recurrent preimplantation embryo arrest). This is the presentation in the founding cohort and in the subcortical-maternal-complex cohort.

nodes.description: Model-derived. Fully grown mouse oocytes normally silence transcription before the oocyte-to-embryo transition, and silencing marks the developmentally competent state. Oocytes lacking Zfp36l2 do not silence transcription, and they then mature and fertilize poorly. Silencing has not been assessed in patient oocytes. No GO term is bound: OLS searches of GO for "transcriptional silencing" and "heterochromatin formation" returned RNA-mediated silencing and heterochromatin-formation terms, none describing global transcriptional silencing of the oocyte.

nodes.description: Mainly model-derived. In growing mouse oocytes lacking Zfp36l2, mRNAs for H3K4 and H3K9 demethylases are not degraded, and the oocyte fails to accumulate H3K4me3 and H3K9me3. Patient ZFP36L2 variants expressed in mouse oocytes also give aberrant H3K4me3 and H3K9me3 levels. Histone marks have not been measured in patient oocytes. No GO term is bound because the GO histone-methylation process terms are obsolete.

nodes.description: Maternal mRNAs that ZFP36L2 would normally degrade persist in patient zygotes, in mouse oocytes expressing patient variants, and in transfected HeLa cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing of patient oocytes shows altered transcripts for cell division, mitochondrial function, and ribosome metabolism. One cohort reports that ZFP36L2 co-precipitates with subcortical maternal complex proteins, but whether that interaction is part of the disease mechanism is not established.
